scale: audience_value and business_value are 0-5 team judgments; cost 0-5; red flags force turned_down

moves.move: Launch the recipe site on WordPress + WP Recipe Maker with her 50 most-saved recipes
moves.first_step: Buy the domain, Kinsta Starter hosting and WP Recipe Maker Premium; install the theme (2 hrs)
moves.done_when: 50 recipe pages pass Google’s Rich Results Test; soft launch Mon Jan 4
moves.why: The #1 priority: recipes trapped in captions get a home she owns. Squarespace and Wix were rejected: no built-in recipe markup for Google. (Product & Tech dept.)

moves.move: Point the Instagram link in bio to the site and add “Full recipe: link in bio” to every Reel
moves.first_step: Write the one-line Reel caption she’ll reuse (5 min)
moves.done_when: Link in bio points to the site; the next 10 Reels carry the line
moves.why: Highest-priority card: zero cost, every follower. Instagram reach per post is falling (vendor data, Market dept.), so owned channels matter.

moves.move: Start the free weekly “What’s for Dinner” email on Kit, with a sign-up under every recipe
moves.first_step: Create the Kit account, an email-only sign-up form and the welcome email (1.5 hrs)
moves.cost_detail: $0 up to 10,000 subscribers (Kit free plan) · 2 hours/week
moves.done_when: Form on every recipe page with double opt-in and one-click unsubscribe; first issue sent
moves.why: The reason to come back every week and a list she owns. Email only, never a gate on recipes. (Product + Market depts.)

moves.move: Log every “what can I use instead?” question
moves.first_step: Start the questions log and copy the last 2 weeks of DM questions into it (1.5 hrs)
moves.done_when: 100+ questions logged and tagged by recipe
moves.why: Phase 1 data: cooks leave when they’re missing something. This log is the seed of Ask Diane.

moves.move: Write the free / book / paid rules and a clean-page standard
moves.first_step: Sort her 20 most popular recipes into Free or Book-only in one sitting (1 hr)
moves.done_when: Signed rule sheet: recipe card on the first screen, no pop-ups, no autoplay sound, book recipes stay in the book
moves.metric_90_day: Zero ad complaints; no book recipe written out in a Reel for 90 days
moves.why: Stops free videos cannibalizing the cookbook and blocks the ad clutter readers complain about (Coalition for Better Ads, Market dept.).

moves.move: Teach the first live online class at $35 per household, 50 seats
moves.first_step: Pick a non-book recipe and a date (30 min)
moves.done_when: Class held; post-class survey sent
moves.why: Priced against Milk Street ($29.95) and Sur La Table ($39/household). Sells what a caption can’t: Diane, live. (Revenue dept.)

moves.move: Send a media kit and recipe-development pitch to 10 food brands she already uses
moves.first_step: Collect dated follower stats and her 5 best brand-fit posts (1.5 hrs)
moves.done_when: Kit sent to 10 brands, every claim dated and sourced
moves.why: Her Whole Foods prepared-foods background is rare among creators. CT Post reports brands already pay her for recipes. Every partnership disclosed (R1).

moves.move: Pilot a Fairfield County corporate cooking event at $150–200 a person ($3K minimum)
moves.first_step: Shortlist 3 local venues with kitchens (1.5 hrs)
moves.done_when: One paid event delivered
moves.why: Benchmarks support $150–175 a person in NYC/CT; a flat $10K was unproven, so the price came down. (Revenue dept.)

moves.move: Launch an optional $7/month meal-plan membership with one-click cancel
moves.first_step: Draft one sample week of meal plan and shopping list (1.5 hrs)
moves.done_when: Live with one-click cancel and a reminder 3 days before any renewal; recipes stay free
moves.why: Priced between NYT Cooking and $5 Meal Plan. Launch only after classes show repeat buyers. No silent trial conversions.

moves.move: Pitch Cookbook #2 with QR links to the site, classes and email
moves.first_step: Pull the 50 most-asked questions and site searches that found nothing (1 hr)
moves.cost_detail: Advance and royalties per contract (ask Diane)
moves.done_when: Proposal sent to the publisher
moves.why: Built from what her cooks actually ask. The book stays a relationship builder.

moves.move: Add an “Out of it? Swap it” box and Recipe markup to every recipe
moves.first_step: Write swap boxes for the top 10 recipes from the questions log (2 hrs)
moves.done_when: All 50 recipes have swap boxes and pass the Rich Results Test
moves.why: Phase 1: cooks leave when they lack something. The answer sits right on the recipe, even before Ask Diane exists. (Market dept.)

moves.move: Add “Cook with what you have” filters: no mixer, one pan, 5 pantry items, meatless
moves.first_step: Tag the 50 recipes by tool and pantry needs in a spreadsheet (2 hrs)
moves.done_when: Filters live on the recipe index
moves.why: Turns “I don’t have it” into “here’s what I can make.”

moves.move: Verify the NYT list claim and date-stamp every follower count
moves.first_step: Ask Diane and Simon & Schuster for the list, week and rank; screenshot each profile with the date (1 hr)
moves.done_when: Fact sheet with a source and date for every claim
moves.metric_90_day: Zero unverified claims in any pitch
moves.why: Scores Extraction risk by the formula: it protects her credibility more than it helps cooks. Kept because it prevents misleading claims in D7. Counts disagree: 1.4M (AARP, Mar 2025), 1.5M (Sep 2025), ~2M undated.

moves.move: Build the Approved Swaps sheet with Diane’s sign-off
moves.first_step: Enter the 10 swaps she answers most often (1 hr)
moves.done_when: ~100 swaps approved
moves.metric_90_day: 80% of Ask Diane questions covered by an approved swap
moves.why: Ask Diane can only give a swap that is on this sheet. This is what keeps it honest.

moves.move: Install Fathom analytics and a 5-metric weekly email
moves.first_step: Install the Fathom script and set up print and save events (1 hr)
moves.done_when: Weekly metrics email reaches Diane
moves.why: Privacy-respecting: no ad tracking. Measures returning visitors, saves, prints, “it worked” ratings and email sign-ups.

moves.move: Adopt a written FTC disclosure and honest-partnership standard
moves.first_step: Draft a one-page policy from the FTC’s Disclosures 101 (1 hr)
moves.done_when: Signed and linked from the media kit
moves.metric_90_day: 100% of sponsored posts carry a spoken and on-screen disclosure
moves.why: FTC guidance: on video the disclosure must be said and shown; a tag behind “more” doesn’t count. Protects her trust before any new deal.

moves.move: Build a one-page rate card for recipe development and brand work
moves.first_step: List Diane’s past paid projects and fees (ask her) (1 hr)
moves.done_when: Rate card with 3 packages: $2.5K / $7.5K / $15K (est.)
moves.why: Studio benchmarks run about $2K per recipe (Heart Creative). Paid recipe work already exists (CT Post).

moves.move: Host an in-person demo at $85 with a book-bundle option
moves.first_step: Ask Diane which local venue or bookstore she prefers (30 min)
moves.done_when: 60 tickets sold and the demo held
moves.why: Sur La Table charges $69–95, so $150 was too high. A mission bet: great for fans, modest money.

moves.move: Turn the recipe site into an installable web app (PWA) before considering a native app
moves.first_step: Ask the site developer to quote add-to-home-screen, offline saved recipes and cook mode (30 min)
moves.cost_detail: $2–5K on top of the site build (est.)
moves.done_when: Readers can install Diane on their phone and open saved recipes offline
moves.why: An app store app costs far more and takes 15–30% of subscriptions; a web app gives cooks saved recipes and cook mode now. Native only after 300+ paying members.

moves.move: Require an email address to see a recipe
moves.first_step: Don’t build. Offer the email after the recipe instead (D3).
moves.why: Breaks the “You Got This!” promise at the first visit.

moves.move: Put display ads above the recipe card
moves.first_step: Don’t build now. Revisit only with strict rules: nothing between the cook and the recipe.
moves.why: No red flag, but the scores say it takes more from cooks than it gives.

moves.move: Turn Instagram captions into recipe cards with the migration agent
moves.first_step: Request Instagram’s “Download Your Information” JSON export and list the top 50 by saves (1 hr)
moves.done_when: 50 recipe cards approved by Diane
moves.why: Uses the data export, not the Graph API (needs a professional account, ~200 calls/hour). Cuts the biggest cost of D1.

moves.move: Sort DMs and email with the inbox sorter
moves.first_step: Export 50 recent DMs and emails and test the sorting prompt (2 hrs)
moves.done_when: Every new message gets a category and a draft reply within a day
moves.metric_90_day: Brand and media replies within 2 business days, 90% of the time (est.)
moves.why: Brand deals stop getting lost; cooking questions feed the swap log.

moves.move: Draft the weekly email with the newsletter drafter
moves.first_step: Feed last week’s recipes into the draft prompt and edit the result (1 hr)
moves.done_when: 4 issues sent from agent drafts
moves.metric_90_day: Diane’s editing time under 30 minutes an issue (est.)
moves.why: Keeps the weekly habit going when Diane is busy.

moves.move: Launch the Ask Diane beta: approved swaps only, human handoff
moves.first_step: Write a one-page spec: guardrails and the handoff (1.5 hrs)
moves.done_when: Passes 50 test prompts (allergens, temperatures, “are you Diane?”) and a WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility check
moves.metric_90_day: 70% answered without handoff; zero unsafe answers
moves.why: Cooks finish dinner with the person they trust. Labeled as AI; never claims to be Diane; uses USDA temperatures; never promises allergen safety.

moves.move: Automate class sign-ups and reminders with the class assistant
moves.first_step: List the 5 emails every class needs (1 hr)
moves.done_when: Sign-up, reminder, shopping list and follow-up send automatically
moves.why: Lets classes grow without more admin time.
